subject: Audit data retention exception — pilot prioritization & product asks
messages:
From: Sara Mehta <sara@medspring.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Josh Klein <josh@innervoice.ai>
Date: 2026-12-13T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Short-term retention exception request for pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo. We have a short follow-up from security and compliance at MedSpring: for the first 3 months of our pilot we need audit log visibility for aggregated request metadata (request ID, model variant, timestamp, routing path) to be retained for 90 days instead of Redwood's standard 30-day window. This is to support a small clinical audit sampling exercise.

Constraints / asks: 
- Data must remain in Redwood's control plane (no third-party mirrors).
- We plan to enable BYOK for model keys in month 2 of the pilot; the retention exception should be independent of BYOK rollout.
- SSO integration (SAML) will be live before pilot start; access to the audit view should honor SSO groups.

Attached is MedSpring's evidence_request_v3 with the exact fields they need. Can you confirm whether this is feasible, what the product trade-offs are, and whether you need any changes from our side to make scope minimal?

Sara
Sara Mehta
Head of Compliance, MedSpring
Attachment: medspring_evidence_request_v3.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mehta <sara@medspring.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-term retention exception request for pilot

Thanks Sara — looping in product + infra + compliance to triage.

Quick clarifying questions before we scope a proposal:
1) Is the 90-day requirement for full request payloads or strictly the audit metadata you listed (request ID, model variant, timestamp, routing path)? Your attachment looks like a mix; we want the minimal set.
2) Is this exception required from day 1 of pilot or can it kick in after a 2-week stabilization window?
3) Do you need row-level access for MedSpring analysts (via UI) or will a periodic CSV export suffice for the sampling exercise?

Initial options we see (tradeoffs below):
A) Policy-only retention extension: extend metadata retention to 90 days in the hosted control plane (fast, low engineering cost; increases storage and audit surface).
B) Scoped, sampled retention: keep full metadata for 90 days but only for a sampled subset of requests (e.g., 10% of traffic or user-tagged requests) — lower cost, more complex UX for tagging/exports.
C) Short-term escrow: export daily audit slices to an internal encrypted bucket (Redwood-managed) for 90 days and allow MedSpring read access via signed links — requires careful KMS/ACL work.

What we need from product/security for a prioritization call:
- Product: which option preserves the best UX for MedSpring and aligns with roadmap (Marissa).
- Infra/Eng: preliminary risk & rough effort estimate (Priyom).
- Compliance: any blocking policy concerns (Naomi, Marcus).

If we can answer Q1–Q3 now I can draft a one-page proposal and timeline for your procurement team.

Laura Bennett
Principal PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-term retention exception request for pilot

Thanks Laura — quick product take: we should avoid a permanent policy change. Option B (scoped, sampled retention) is our preferred path because it balances cost and auditability and fits an incremental rollout. Key product asks to make B workable: 
- Simple tagging mechanism (api header or query flag) for MedSpring to mark pilot requests.
- Admin UI filter to pull sampled records and export CSV with the fields Sara listed.
- Default sample rate 10% with ability to request higher for a limited window (support ticket).

Tradeoffs:
- Lift: medium (backend capture + UI filter + export).
- UX: MedSpring will need a clear way to tag or we will have to instrument proxy rules.
- Compliance: ensure sampled sets still meet audit chain (no anonymization of request IDs).

I'm attaching a proto retention matrix (proto-retention-matrix.xlsx) that maps a minimal field set and the engineering surface. Priyom — can you give a rough estimate (T-shirt) for B vs A vs C? Naomi/Marcus, flag any policy blockers for sampled exports.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proto-retention-matrix.xlsx
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-term retention exception request for pilot

Folks — quick engineering assessment and proposed next steps after reviewing the matrix and Sara's asks.

Summary of feasibility:
- Option A (policy-only): low engineering effort (2w dev + 1w QA) but increases retention footprint and requires updating retention enforcement policies and billing/quotas documentation.
- Option B (scoped sampling): medium effort (3–4w dev + 1w QA) to support tagging ingestion, sample routing, storage labels, plus UI filter/export. Lowest long-term cost and reversible; recommended default.
- Option C (escrow export): highest effort (4–6w + infra approvals) and operational overhead (bucket management, signed links), but keeps retention out of primary control plane.

Risks/notes:
- BYOK independence: we can keep retention policy independent of CMK rotation. BYOK affects keys at rest; retention metadata can be stored encrypted under Redwood-managed keys during pilot, then rotated to customer-managed keys when BYOK is live if required.
- SSO: we will enforce SSO group-based access on the export UI. Work required: map MedSpring groups to our RBAC (1w config).

Proposed delivery plan (if we go with B):
- Dec 20: finalize scope & sample rate (owner: Laura).
- Jan 4: dev kickoff; feature branch for tagging ingestion & sample router (owner: Priyom).
- Jan 25: UI filter + export + compliance audit checks (owner: Marissa).
- Feb 1: internal security review & deploy to staging (owner: Marcus/Naomi).
- Feb 8: pilot roll — sample rate at 10% and monitoring (owner: MedSpring + Redwood CS).

Action items:
- Laura: confirm minimal field set (reply to Sara) by EOD Dec 17.
- Marissa: finalize UX wire (Dec 19) and share with Sara for sign-off.
- Marcus/Naomi: list any compliance blockers for sampled exports (Dec 18).
- Priyom: provide a JIRA epic and rough story point estimate by Dec 19.

I'll open the epic and add the initial spike for ingestion changes. If anyone sees a blocker to the timeline call it out now; otherwise we'll proceed to scope option B for procurement.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Engineering Manager, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
